title: onprem: airgap installer - offline bundles, vendored deps, kube-distro compatibility
author: Asha Patel
description: Add comprehensive support for air-gapped/on-prem private installer: introduce offline bundle generator, vendor critical container images and helm charts, add kube-distro compatibility layer (RKE2, K3s, OpenShift), and improve upgrade/rollback hooks for disconnected environments. This PR implements: 1) offline-bundle CLI (redwood-private-installer bundle create) that collects manifests, images, charts, and config templates into a signed tarball with metadata and checksum; 2) vendoring pipeline (ci/jobs/vendor-offline) that mirrors required images and helm charts into a vendor/ directory and generates an image-mapping YAML used by the installer; 3) kube-distro adapter that applies small patches and RBAC tweaks for OpenShift and K3s (service account annotations, SCC -> SecurityContext constraints notes), and a distro detection heuristic; 4) upgrade/rollback improvements that stage bundles to a local registry and perform atomic helm rollbacks using preflight checks when no outbound network exists; 5) docs and examples for on-prem operators and a quickstart for air-gapped installs. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in regulated or air-gapped sites required a reproducible offline workflow and clear distro-specific mappings. This unblocks several enterprise POCs that cannot access public registries. Related: ENG-3571, SUP-4821. Checklist: - [x] offline bundle format and CLI - [x] vendored artifacts in repo for CI testing - [x] distro adapter hooks for RKE2/K3s/OpenShift - [x] upgrade/rollback smoke tests (integration job) - [x] docs/quickstart updates - [x] signatures+checksum verification in installer UX Notes: bundle format is intentionally conservative (tar.gz of images/helm/manifests + manifest.json). The installer supports loading a local OCI registry tar using skopeo-migrator step or droplet import. This does not change hosted product code paths.
